issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) requires the Animal class to expose its name getter and setter with protected visibility (UML shows '#' and the text explicitly states to implement the name getter and setter with protected visibility). It also shows the Animal constructor as protected in the UML. The solution implementation makes the Animal constructor and the getName()/setName() methods public. This is a visibility mismatch that can confuse students: the textual instructions expect protected access for the getter/setter (and UML shows a protected constructor), but the reference solution uses public methods/constructor. Students following the instruction to make the getter/setter (and constructor) protected may find the solution differing from the reference and tests may assert visibility requirements, causing unexpected failures or confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal class API consistent with the problem statement: change the Animal constructor and the name getter and setter to protected (instead of public) in the reference solution, or alternatively update the problem statement/UML to explicitly allow public visibility. Ensure the chosen visibility is consistently documented in the problem text, UML, template stubs, and reference solution so students are not confused.
